summary: Open-source memory platform that gives AI agents long-term memory by building a knowledge graph from your data.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Cognee is an open-source AI memory platform for agents. It turns text and documents into a knowledge graph plus embeddings, so agents can remember facts and recall the relevant source later.
sixtySeconds.problem: Agents forget between sessions and plain vector search loses how facts relate. Cognee stores memory as a graph you can query.
whoFor: RAG builders who want graph retrieval
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a simple remember and recall API that even runs locally without an LLM key, using a local extraction model.

overview: Install with pip or uv. The gliner extra adds a local extraction model used when no LLM key is set.

With no key, Cognee extracts the graph with GLiNER and embeds locally; both models download on first use. Call cognee.remember with text and a dataset name, then cognee.recall with a question to get matching source text.
Add an LLM key to get generated answers and richer extraction. Cognee is Apache 2.0 licensed.
limitations: Local mode returns source text, not generated answers

firstRun.title: Remember and recall a fact
firstRun.code:
import asyncio
import cognee

async def main():
    await cognee.remember(
        "Marie Curie was born in Warsaw and worked at the University of Paris.",
        dataset_name="local_quickstart",
    )
    results = await cognee.recall(
        "Where was Marie Curie born?",
        datasets=["local_quickstart"],
    )
    for result in results:
        print(result)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
